content.text:
Reading the structure region by region, from left to right:

1. **Cyclopropyl ether:** a 1-methylcyclopropyl group is attached through an oxygen: CC1(CC1)O-.
2. **Indazole:** a 2H-indazole whose benzo ring carries the ether oxygen at C5. C3 of the indazole bears the pyrimidine. The drawn tautomer has N1 with no hydrogen and N2 as NH, so the SMILES is c1(...)[nH]nc2ccc(OC3(C)CC3)cc12.
3. **Pyrimidine:** a pyrimidin-4-yl group attached at C4 to the indazole C3. The ring runs C4, C5(H), C6, N1, C2(H), N3. C6 bears the azetidine nitrogen.
4. **Azetidine:** N-linked, with C3 carrying both F and a CH2 group.
5. **Piperazine:** the CH2 from the azetidine C3 goes to one piperazine nitrogen. The other piperazine nitrogen carries CH2 linked to piperidine C4.
6. **Piperidine:** its nitrogen is attached to C5 of the isoindoline-1,3-dione.
7. **Glutarimide:** the isoindoline nitrogen is bonded to the 3-position of a 2,6-dioxopiperidine. This stereocentre is drawn with plain bonds, so no stereo is given.

Assembled SMILES:

CC1(CC1)Oc1ccc2n[nH]c(c2c1)-c1cc(ncn1)N1CC(F)(C1)CN1CCN(CC1)CC1CCN(CC1)c1ccc2C(=O)N(C3CCC(=O)NC3=O)C(=O)c2c1

Checking the indazole: c1ccc2n[nH]c(c2c1) with the ether on c1. The atom order is c1 (OR), c, c, c2 (C7a), n (N1), [nH] (N2), c (C3), c2 (C3a), c1 (C4). C4 closes the ring back to the ether-bearing carbon, which makes that carbon C5. This matches the drawing.

Checking the isoindoline: c1ccc2C(=O)N(...)C(=O)c2c1, where the first c1 is attached to the piperidine nitrogen. The ring atoms are c1 (N-attached), c, c, c2 (bearing C=O), then the imide, then c2 and c1. The last aromatic CH sits between the piperidine-bearing carbon and the carbonyl-bearing carbon, which matches the drawing, where the substituent is at position 5.

SMILES: CC1(CC1)Oc1ccc2n[nH]c(c2c1)-c1cc(ncn1)N1CC(F)(C1)CN1CCN(CC1)CC1CCN(CC1)c1ccc2C(=O)N(C3CCC(=O)NC3=O)C(=O)c2c1
